How much slope should a court have?
text: We build about 99% of our courts at 1%, or 1 inch every 10 feet. That's about 3.6 inches across a 30-foot court. Flatter still drains, but slower: more ponding, more squeegeeing and more dirt staining.

title: Portable pickleball net or in-ground posts?
text: Modern aluminum portable nets weigh 30 to 40 pounds, cost less, and kids can move them. The tension is a little looser. If you play a lot, in-ground posts are best. Skip the sleeves and you can still core holes later.

title: Can we pour the slab now and add a shade structure later?

When can you paint the court? Why not in winter?
text: A new slab needs at least 30 days to cure, and then the ground has to warm up and dry out. A slab poured in December usually gets coated in February or March. In the meantime we can put up the fence, nets and even temporary lines so you can play.

title: What should go right up against the court edge?
text: Treat acrylic like stucco. Keep grass, mulch and beds about 2 inches below the court surface, or use a rock border, so water can't wick under the coating and peel it. Pavers can be flush. Avoid fine quarter-inch decomposed granite: it tracks onto the court and scratches it.

title: Can we sell sponsor or donor names on the court to fundraise?

Is it hard to tell if the ball is in or out on a one-color court?
text: No. Your eye reads the yellow ball against the white line, not against the court color. An all-one-color court with white lines plays fine. Dark or colored lines are what make calls hard.

title: Square posts or round posts? Do we need a top rail?
text: Round. If someone runs into a post, they hit a blunt surface instead of a corner, and that's why sports construction standards use round posts. Get a top rail too. Without one, the fence bends when players run into it.

title: Do fence-mounted light bars work as well as poles for tennis?
text: For many courts, yes. Light bars mount on the fence and aim down, so neighbors see a hard edge of darkness, and nothing on the ends blinds the server. They're great for retrofits. For poles, three is good recreational light, four is better and six is tournament level.
